rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a physical house or other building, including a non-residential one when the context makes that clear.

example.english: This house used to be a clinic.
example.traditional: 呢間屋以前係診所嚟㗎。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 uk1 ji5 cin4 hai6 zan2 so2 lei4 gaa3

rows.note: Use this for physically keeping an object at or inside a particular place, such as a car in a garage.

example.english: We house the car in the garage.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 zoeng1 gaa3 ce1 fong3 hai2 ce1 fong2

rows.note: Use this when admitting someone to stay with you or giving them shelter.

example.english: We house someone who has to sleep on the street.
example.traditional: 我哋收留咗個要瞓街嘅人。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 sau1 lau4 zo2 go3 jiu1 fan3 gaai1 ge3 jan4

rows.note: Use this for the people making up a household, especially when referring to them as a family living together.

example.english: Everyone in our house eats dinner together every night.
example.traditional: 我哋一家人每晚都一齊食飯。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 jat1 gaa1 jan4 mui5 maan5 dou1 jat1 cai4 sik6 faan6

rows.note: Use this in the legislative context for a parliamentary chamber or the legislative body represented by it.

example.english: The new bill will be voted on in the house next week.
example.traditional: 新法案下星期會喺議院表決。
example.jyutping: san1 faat3 on3 haa6 sing1 kei4 wui5 hai2 ji5 jyun2 biu2 kyut3
